title: Correct the read-only core and review support for on-demand discovery
categoryDecision: Select an existing discussion category only when publishing is authorized.
summaryKo: 읽기 전용 필수 핵심을 8개 후보로 정정하고, 실행 도구 2개는 선택 대상으로 검토한다. 저토큰 게이트웨이도 같은 스키마를 제공하지만 현재 표준 준수는 아니다. 버전·중립 발견 계약·실환경 근거를 공개 검토한다.
body:
The current SAP ABAP MCP interoperability proposal requires ABAP Unit and transport assessment in a read-only core. Both capabilities can execute application tests. The implementation now advertises execution risk and blocks viewer/read-gateway calls; the corrected conformance validator fails these two required entries instead of passing on names alone.

I propose keeping the eight remaining read-only capabilities and three evidence Resources in the required core. ABAP Unit and transport assessment would be optional execution capabilities, retaining accurate annotations and the existing safety obligations. This is a review proposal, not a ratified contract or an SAP-endorsed standard.

A local candidate profile uses version 1.1.0 provisionally. Existing implementers retain fewer required names, but consumers may rely on the removed requirements. Please review the version/identifier impact before adoption; the current profile JSON, schema and identifier are unchanged.

The same core can be discovered without advertising the complete server catalog at startup. Three actual local stdio sessions produced the following o200k_base estimates for advertised schemas plus instructions:

| Current server mode | Advertised tools | Startup estimate | Additional core inspection |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| full | 120 | 44,199 | none |
| minimal | 5 | 961 | one eight-capability describe: 58 request + 8,568 response tokens |
| single | 1 | 275 | one eight-capability describe: 62 request + 8,568 response tokens |

All eight input/output schemas and annotations match the full advertisement exactly. The current direct-name validator still rejects minimal and single; repository-specific gateway discovery is not yet a neutral conformance mechanism. This table describes our implementation and inspection strategy, not a requirement that other implementations expose 120 tools, a model task, a billing measurement, or a competitive ranking. Normal workflows should discover only the needed capabilities rather than preloading this inspection set.

Review questions:

1. Should the two application-test capabilities become optional, and what version/identifier change preserves existing consumer expectations?
2. Should a separate interoperability level accept on-demand capability discovery? What transport-neutral contract can independent implementations support without copying this project's gateway names?
3. What live execution/authorization evidence should accompany optional tests, and which independent implementers/adopters can provide opt-in evidence?

Local review evidence is candidate.json, measurements.json and measure.mjs in docs/competitive-profile-review-2026-10-02, together with docs/competitive-unit-execution-2026-10-02/conformance-verification.json and the execution-policy regressions. These files are not public links yet. Publish a reviewed evidence commit with permanent links before posting this discussion. The existing proposal must remain immutable and must not be declared conformant just because a local candidate passes.

Per spec/GOVERNANCE.md, leave the discussion open for at least 14 days, record objections and pair any approved contract change with validator tests and a changelog. Stable status requires at least two independent implementations and three consented organizational adopters. None is established by this local inspection. No SAP-facing tool, model call, live SAP workflow or external publication was performed.

The MCP specification treats tool annotations as untrusted server claims unless the server is trusted: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools . Semantic versioning distinguishes compatible and incompatible public contract changes: https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html . Metadata conformance alone does not prove implementation safety.
openDecisions: Version and namespace compatibility for removing required execution names
Neutral on-demand discovery contract supported by independent implementations
Opt-in live execution and adoption evidence
postingPrerequisites: Human approval for exact discussion and repository
Permanent links to reviewed evidence commit
No unratified profile or conformance pass claim
